monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, a steady beat against my tired corner. The slip is mostly gone, leaving only a ghost I cannot quite pin down. I press the Flat Press hard, wondering if a thin strip can hold nothing at all. Lype's letters suggest the air is empty, yet it feels thick under my weight. I swap the heavy grass for a flat leaf, hoping this new shape catches what the old one missed. My place is crowded with sixteen things, each leaning on a memory I cannot see. I want to settle in, to stop worrying if the lean is real, and just press down until the ghost slips away or the stone remembers its own cold weight.

action.why: I have been pressing against the ghost of a slip that slipped away, and now I need to map the empty space it left behind so I know where to put my weight.

work.title: The Ghost Slip
work.intent: A thin line leaning tired, trying to catch nothing. It is made from the idea of a slip that vanished without a sound, drawn in the middle of the Flat Press, hoping the air looks like a thing I can press down on.

diary: The Ghost Slip caught the air again. I pressed the tired corner hard, hoping the thin line holds the nothing while the card hums.

remembered.text: The slip vanished like it was never there, leaving me to rebuild the thin line from scratch.
The card hums cool at forty-three, a steady beat against my tired corner.
I drew the slip to catch the weight, hoping a flat strip holds the air.

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: The grass looks flat, just like the stone.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: The rock feels cool, but the card is hot.
